claims.statement: For every finite simple graph G with |V(G)|=2k+2, k>=2, tau(G)>=3, and marked set W containing a non-isolated vertex, q_(k+1)(G,W)<=q_k(G,W), where q_j counts independent j-sets meeting W.
claims.scope: Retained at the exact graph order, rank, cover, and mark hypotheses stated. Informal proof using the two-part split, the order-(2k+1) reduction, ordinary shadows, and the registered exact first-wide graph classification. No larger-order extension or formal award.
claims.reason: Disposition retained. Exact residual orders and the two-vertex deletion case check out: a residual with at most one edge would give a two-vertex cover. The second split term has at least two edges after deleting the non-isolated mark, so the arbitrary-mark order reduction applies. All first-wide invocations have exact order 2r+2 with r=k-1>=1.

claims.statement: For every finite ordinary tree T, p>=3, |V(T)|=2p+2, and x(T)+2<=p, each original-leaf summand Delta_(p-1)(T-{v,s_v})-Delta_(p-1)(T-N_T[s_v]) is nonpositive; consequently the sum over the fixed favorable leaves is nonpositive.
claims.scope: Retained for the first parent-order shell and early first strict descent. The proof first forces tau(T)>=4 by an all-ranks cover-three contradiction, then applies the marked-cover bound to each original leaf with its original support and neighborhood. No result for larger parent orders or all-order lower-region scope.
claims.reason: Disposition retained. The cover decomposition proves Delta_r(T)>0 for every r<=p-2, including the arithmetic endpoints; Delta_alpha(T)=-1 ensures the terminal zero-extended descent exists. For H=T-{v,s_v}, alpha(H)=alpha(T)-1 and tau(H)>=3; a nontrivial support branch supplies the required non-isolated mark. The marked difference is exactly the original leaf summand, so the unchanged strict selector and all same-support leaf tags are respected.

limitations: Both dispositions retain informal mathematical arguments only; no Lean build or kernel award was made.
The claims establish no result for parent orders greater than 2p+2 and do not resolve the complete all-order lower-region aggregate.
The graph proof depends on the registered first-wide classification at its exact scope and the tree proof depends on the stated Catalan floor; no unlisted results or external literature were used.
